chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Bundar, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdillah, from a number of our companions, from al-Hasan ibn Ali ibn Yusuf al-Azdi, from a man, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man came to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) and said to him, 'I have never kissed a child.' When he turned away, the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said, 'This man is with us [considered] to be from the people of Hell.'
ai.seo_question: Why did the Prophet declare a man who never kissed a child to be from the people of Hell?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, the Prophet Muhammad identifies the lack of kissing a child not merely as a social oversight, but as a profound spiritual deficiency indicative of a cold heart, leading to the verdict of being 'from the people of Hell.' This reflects the Shia emphasis on *mawadda* (affection) and natural tenderness (*fitra*) as essential components of faith and emotional health. The narration underscores that physical expressions of love are outward manifestations of inner spiritual vitality.
